doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: NEA Jazz Master, family and the future
title: Closing thanks to the Smithsonian and end of interview
summary: Walton thanks Brower and Kimery and the Smithsonian archive, jokes about faxes and Jazz Masters funders, and says the interview sets the record straight.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

Cedar Anthony Walton.

Uh of the Smithsonian because it's a very important uh uh uh place in our country that preserves uh things that uh uh the Institute itself uh uh considers valuable and uh uh … uh historic enough uh to uh preserve. So, I'm grateful to be able to speak on my, on behalf in this context. No.
No? Okay.
No, I, I would hope that we've opened a door that we could continue to walk through.
Oh, to add to this. Oh man.

Uh-huh.

Right. Uh-huh. Well, I've certainly uh found uh this to be a, a surprisingly uh, uh, uh pleasant opportunity for me to uh express myself from the beginning of my uh music uh explorations to the present time. And I think it's very fortunate that I was able, to be able to perform here in uh Washington, D.C. and uh for you to uh be able to witness that too, and we can use that as a point of reference, which is, gives it a new uh, I mean a, a nice uh point of view, vantage point, I think.
